Calakmul.fact: Calakmul is estimated to have had a population of 50,000 people and had governance, at times, over places as far away as 150 kilometers (93 mi).

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: There are _____ ancient structures identified at Calakmul, the largest of which is the great pyramid at the site
Calakmul.fact: There are 6,750 ancient structures identified at Calakmul, the largest of which is the great pyramid at the site.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Structure 2 is over _____ (148 ft) high, making it one of the tallest of the Mesoamerican pyramids
Calakmul.fact: Structure 2 is over 45 metres (148 ft) high, making it one of the tallest of the Mesoamerican pyramids.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The ruins of El Tintal are _____ (42 mi) to the southwest of Calakmul and were linked to both El Mirador and Calakmul itself by causeway
Calakmul.fact: The ruins of El Tintal are 68 kilometres (42 mi) to the southwest of Calakmul and were linked to both El Mirador and Calakmul itself by causeway.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Calakmul was about _____ (12 mi) south of the contemporary city of Oxpemul and approximately 25 kilometres (16 mi) southwest of La Muñeca
Calakmul.fact: Calakmul was about 20 kilometres (12 mi) south of the contemporary city of Oxpemul and approximately 25 kilometres (16 mi) southwest of La Muñeca.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The city is located on a rise about _____ (115 ft) above a large seasonal swamp lying to the west, known as the El Laberinto bajo (a Spanish word used in the region to denote a low-lying area of seaso
Calakmul.fact: The city is located on a rise about 35 metres (115 ft) above a large seasonal swamp lying to the west, called the El Laberinto bajo (a Spanish word used in the region to denote a low-lying area of seasonal marshland).

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: This swamp measures approximately 34 by _____ (21.1 by 5.0 mi) and was an important source of water during the rainy season
Calakmul.fact: The ruins of El Tintal are 68 kilometres (42 mi) to the southwest of Calakmul and were linked to both El Mirador and Calakmul itself by causeway. This swamp measures approximately 34 by 8 kilometres (21.1 by 5.0 mi) and was an important source of water during the rainy season.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The city is situated on a promontory formed by a natural 35-metre (_____) high limestone dome rising above the surrounding lowlands
Calakmul.fact: The city is situated on a promontory formed by a natural 35-metre (115 ft) high limestone dome rising above the surrounding lowlands.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The total rural population of the kingdom is calculated at _____ people
Calakmul.fact: The total rural population of the kingdom is calculated at 1.5 million people.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The entire population of the Calakmul kingdom, including the city itself and the rural population in the 13,000 square kilometres (5,000 sq mi) area of the regional state, is calculated at _____ peopl
Calakmul.fact: The entire population of the Calakmul kingdom, including the city itself and the rural population in the 13,000 square kilometres (5,000 sq mi) area of the regional state, is calculated at 1.75 million people in the Late Classic period.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: At times the city had governance over places as far away as _____
Calakmul.fact: At times the city had governance over places as far away as 150 kilometers.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Earlier times tended to be dominated by a single larger city and by the _____ was moving into this position after the dominance of El Mirador in the Late Preclassic and Nakbe in the Middle Preclassic
Calakmul.fact: Earlier times tended to be dominated by a single larger city and by the Early Classic Tikal was moving into this position after the dominance of El Mirador in the Late Preclassic and Nakbe in the Middle Preclassic.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Eventually both cities succumbed to the spreading _____ collapse
Calakmul.fact: Eventually both cities succumbed to the spreading Classic Maya collapse.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: This dynasty has been reconstructed in part from _____ ceramics from the region of great Preclassic cities of El Mirador and Nakbe
Calakmul.fact: This dynasty has been reconstructed in part from Late Classic ceramics from the region of great Preclassic cities of El Mirador and Nakbe.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: After this there is a gap in the hieroglyphic records that lasts over a century, although the _____ dynasty experienced a major expansion of its power at this time
Calakmul.fact: After this there is a gap in the hieroglyphic records that lasts over a century, although the Kaan dynasty experienced a major expansion of its power at this time. The lack of inscriptions recording the events of this period may be either due to the fact that the Kaan dynasty was located elsewhere during this time or perhaps that the monuments were later destroyed.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The nearby _____ site of El Resbalón has a jumbled hieroglyphic text, including a date in 529, that indicates that the city was within the control of the Kaan dynasty
Calakmul.fact: The earliest legible texts referring to the kings of the Kaan dynasty come from excavations of the large city of Dzibanche in Quintana Roo, far north of Calakmul. The nearby Quintana Roo site of El Resbalón has a jumbled hieroglyphic text, including a date in 529, that indicates that the city was within the control of the Kaan dynasty.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Another vassal of Tuun K'ab' Hix was taken captive by _____ on the banks of the Usumacinta River in 537
Calakmul.fact: Another vassal of Tuun K'ab' Hix was taken captive by Yaxchilan on the banks of the Usumacinta River in 537.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In 561, the king now known as _____ installed a ruler at the site of Los Alacranes
Calakmul.fact: In 561, the king now called Sky Witness installed a ruler at the site of Los Alacranes. Sky Witness played a major part in the political events of the Maya region.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In 562, according to a damaged text at Caracol, _____ defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king Wak Chan K'awiil, thus ending his branch of the royal dynasty at Tikal
Calakmul.fact: In 561, the king now called Sky Witness installed a ruler at the site of Los Alacranes. Sky Witness played a major part in the political events of the Maya region.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sky Witness played a major part in the political events of the _____ region
Calakmul.fact: Sky Witness played a major part in the political events of the Maya region.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: He became the overlord of the city of _____, to the south of Naranjo, which had previously been a vassal of Tikal
Calakmul.fact: He became the overlord of the city of Caracol, to the south of Naranjo, which had previously been a vassal of Tikal. In 562, according to a damaged text at Caracol, Sky Witness defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king Wak Chan K'awiil, thus ending his branch of the royal dynasty at Tikal.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: This event is used as a marker to divide the _____ from the Late Classic
Calakmul.fact: This event is used as a marker to divide the Early Classic from the Late Classic.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sky Witness is also mentioned at Okop, a site much further north in _____
Calakmul.fact: Sky Witness is also mentioned at Okop, a site much further north in Quintana Roo.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The last reference to _____ occurs at Caracol and is dated to AD 572
Calakmul.fact: Sky Witness is also mentioned at Okop, a site much further north in Quintana Roo. The last reference to Sky Witness occurs at Caracol and is dated to AD 572.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Uneh Chan maintained his alliances with cities in the east and he is depicted on _____ 4 supervising an event involving king Yajaw Te' K'inich of that city that occurred before 583
Calakmul.fact: Uneh Chan maintained his alliances with cities in the east and he is depicted on Caracol Stela 4 supervising an event involving king Yajaw Te' K'inich of that city that occurred before 583.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Janab Pakal died in March 612 and _____ a few months later
Calakmul.fact: Palenque was now ruled by king Ajen Yohl Mat who had gained some sort of independence from Calakmul, provoking the new invasion. The immediate aftermath of this second victory over Palenque involved the deaths of the two most important nobles at the city, Ajen Yohl Mat himself and Janab Pakal, a high-ranking member of the royal family and possibly co-ruler.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The wars against _____ may have been undertaken by Uneh Chan in order to seize control of wealthy trade routes that passed through the western Maya region
Calakmul.fact: Palenque suffered a lengthy decline in its fortunes after this date before it was able to recover from its disastrous war with Calakmul. The wars against Palenque may have been undertaken by Uneh Chan in order to seize control of wealthy trade routes that passed through the western Maya region.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Yuknoom Head conquered another city in _____ 636, although the exact site is unknown
Calakmul.fact: Yuknoom Head conquered another city in March 636, although the exact site is unknown.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: B'alaj _____ K'awiil was installed on the throne of the new outpost at the age of four, in 635, and for many years served as a loyal vassal fighting for his brother, the king of Tikal
Calakmul.fact: B'alaj Chan K'awiil was installed on the throne of the new outpost at the age of four, in 635, and for many years served as a loyal vassal fighting for his brother, the king of Tikal. B'alaj Chan K'awiil was captured by Yuknoom Che'en II but, instead of being sacrificed, he was re-instated on his throne as a vassal of the Calakmul king, and went on to attack Tikal in 657, forcing Nuun Ujol Chaak, the then king of Tikal, to temporarily abandon the city.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The first two rulers of _____ continued to use the Mutal emblem glyph of Tikal, and they probably felt that they had a legitimate claim to the throne of Tikal itself
Calakmul.fact: In AD 648 Calakmul attacked Dos Pilas and gained an overwhelming victory that included the death of a Tikal lord. The first two rulers of Dos Pilas continued to use the Mutal emblem glyph of Tikal, and they probably felt that they had a legitimate claim to the throne of Tikal itself.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: For some reason, B'alaj Chan K'awiil was not installed as the new ruler of Tikal; instead he stayed at _____
Calakmul.fact: In AD 648 Calakmul attacked Dos Pilas and gained an overwhelming victory that included the death of a Tikal lord. The first two rulers of Dos Pilas continued to use the Mutal emblem glyph of Tikal, and they probably felt that they had a legitimate claim to the throne of Tikal itself.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Tikal counterattacked against _____ in 672, driving B'alaj Chan K'awiil into an exile that lasted five years
Calakmul.fact: The first two rulers of Dos Pilas continued to use the Mutal emblem glyph of Tikal, and they probably felt that they had a legitimate claim to the throne of Tikal itself. For some reason, B'alaj Chan K'awiil was not installed as the new ruler of Tikal; instead he stayed at Dos Pilas.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Troubles continued in the east, with renewed conflict between _____ and Caracol
Calakmul.fact: Troubles continued in the east, with renewed conflict between Naranjo and Caracol. Naranjo completely defeated Caracol in 680 but Naranjo's dynasty disappeared within two years and a daughter of B'alaj Chan K'awiil set up a new dynasty there in 682, indicating that Calakmul had probably intervened decisively to place a loyal vassal on the throne.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Yuknoom Che'en II commanded the loyalty of three generations of kings at Cancuen, _____ (152 mi) to the south, and supervised the enthronement of at least two of them, in 656 and 677
Calakmul.fact: Yuknoom Che'en II commanded the loyalty of three generations of kings at Cancuen, 245 kilometres (152 mi) to the south, and supervised the enthronement of at least two of them, in 656 and 677.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: He already held high office before he was named king and may have been responsible for the major successes of the latter part of _____'en II's reign
Calakmul.fact: Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ak' succeeded Yuknoom Che'en II, his crowning on 3 April 686 was recorded on monuments at Dos Pilas and El Peru. He already held high office before he was named king and may have been responsible for the major successes of the latter part of Yuknoom Che'en II's reign.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Just four years later, in _____ 695, the two states were once again at war
Calakmul.fact: Just four years later, in August 695, the two states were once again at war.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: No stelae remain standing in the site core recording _____'aal K'ak, although there are some in the Northeast Group and 2 broken stelae were buried in Structure 2
Calakmul.fact: Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ak' led his warriors against Jasaw Chan K'awiil I in a catastrophic battle that saw the defeat of Calakmul and the capture of the image of a Calakmul deity named Yajaw Maan. It is unknown what happened to Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ak'; a stucco sculpture from Tikal shows a captive and the king is mentioned in the accompanying caption but it is not certain if the captive and the king are the same person.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: A partial reading of his name is _____' K'awiil
Calakmul.fact: A partial reading of his name is Yuknoom Took' K'awiil. El Peru also continued as a vassal and Yuknoom Took' K'awiil installed a new king there at an unknown date.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: El Peru also continued as a vassal and _____' K'awiil installed a new king there at an unknown date
Calakmul.fact: A partial reading of his name is Yuknoom Took' K'awiil. El Peru also continued as a vassal and Yuknoom Took' K'awiil installed a new king there at an unknown date.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Wamaw K'awiil is named at _____á on the southern periphery of Mesoamerica
Calakmul.fact: Wamaw K'awiil is named at Quiriguá on the southern periphery of Mesoamerica. Quiriguá traditionally had been a vassal of its southern neighbour Copán, and in 724 Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil, king of Copán, installed K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat upon Quiriguá's throne as his vassal.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In _____, only two years later, K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat received a visit from Wamaw K'awiil of Calakmul, while Copán was one of Tikal's oldest allies
Calakmul.fact: In 736, only two years later, K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat received a visit from Wamaw K'awiil of Calakmul, while Copán was one of Tikal's oldest allies.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In 738 K'ak' _____ captured the powerful but elderly king of Copán, Uaxaclajuun Ub'aah K'awiil
Calakmul.fact: The timing of this visit by the king of Calakmul is highly significant, falling between the accession of K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat to the throne of Quiriguá as a vassal of Copán and the outright rebellion that was to follow. It is likely that contact with Calakmul had been initiated soon after K'ak' Tiliw Chan Yopaat acceded to the throne.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: An inscription at _____á, although difficult to interpret, suggests that the capture took place on 27 April 738, when Quiriguá seized and burned the wooden images of Copán's patron deities
Calakmul.fact: This strongly suggests that Calakmul sponsored Quiriguá's rebellion in order to weaken Tikal and to gain access to the rich trade route of the Motagua Valley. An inscription at Quiriguá, although difficult to interpret, suggests that the capture took place on 27 April 738, when Quiriguá seized and burned the wooden images of Copán's patron deities.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The captured lord was taken back to _____á and on 3 May 738 he was decapitated in a public ritual
Calakmul.fact: An inscription at Quiriguá, although difficult to interpret, suggests that the capture took place on 27 April 738, when Quiriguá seized and burned the wooden images of Copán's patron deities. The captured lord was taken back to Quiriguá and on 3 May 738 he was decapitated in a public ritual.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In 751 _____ Z erected a stela that was never finished, paired with another with the portrait of a queen
Calakmul.fact: In 751 Ruler Z erected a stela that was never finished, paired with another with the portrait of a queen.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: B'olon K'awiil was king by 771 when he raised two stelae and he was mentioned at _____á in 789
Calakmul.fact: B'olon K'awiil was king by 771 when he raised two stelae and he was mentioned at Toniná in 789.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: This was a process that paralleled events at _____
Calakmul.fact: This was a process that paralleled events at Tikal.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: A few monuments appear to be even later although their style is crude, representing the efforts of a remnant population to maintain the _____ tradition
Calakmul.fact: A few monuments appear to be even later although their style is crude, representing the efforts of a remnant population to maintain the Classic Maya tradition.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: A year later he informed _____ of the site's existence and the presence of more than 60 stelae
Calakmul.fact: A year later he informed Sylvanus Morley of the site's existence and the presence of more than 60 stelae.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Morley visited the ruins himself on behalf of the Carnegie Institution of Washington in _____
Calakmul.fact: Morley visited the ruins himself on behalf of the Carnegie Institution of Washington in 1932.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Investigations stopped in _____ and archaeologists did not return to the site until 1982 when William J. Folan directed a project on behalf of the Universidad Autónoma de Campeche, working at Calakmul
Calakmul.fact: Investigations stopped in 1938 and archaeologists did not return to the site until 1982 when William J. Folan directed a project on behalf of the Universidad Autónoma de Campeche, working at Calakmul until 1994.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The city's core was bordered on the north side by a 6-metre (_____) high wall that controlled access from the north and may also have had a defensive function
Calakmul.fact: The city's core was bordered on the north side by a 6-metre (20 ft) high wall that controlled access from the north and may also have had a defensive function.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Many commoners residences were built along the edge of _____ swamp to the west of the site core, although some high-status residences and public buildings were interspersed among these
Calakmul.fact: Many commoners residences were built along the edge of El Laberinto swamp to the west of the site core, although some high-status residences and public buildings were interspersed among these.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: There are five major reservoirs, including the largest example in the Maya world, measuring 242 by _____ (794 by 696 ft)
Calakmul.fact: There are five major reservoirs, including the largest example in the Maya world, measuring 242 by 212 metres (794 by 696 ft).

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Aguada 1 is the largest of the reservoirs and has a surface area of _____ (540,000 sq ft)
Calakmul.fact: Aguada 1 is the largest of the reservoirs and has a surface area of 5 hectares (540,000 sq ft).

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: They have been numbered as _____ 1 through to Sacbe 7
Calakmul.fact: They have been numbered as Sacbe 1 through to Sacbe 7. Sacbe 1 is 450 metres (1,480 ft) long and is lined and filled with stone.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sacbe 1 is _____ (1,480 ft) long and is lined and filled with stone
Calakmul.fact: Sacbe 1 is 450 metres (1,480 ft) long and is lined and filled with stone.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sacbe _____ was first mapped in the 1930s by the Carnegie Institution of Washington
Calakmul.fact: Sacbe 1 is 450 metres (1,480 ft) long and is lined and filled with stone. Sacbe 1 was first mapped in the 1930s by the Carnegie Institution of Washington.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: This causeway may have been built to transport stone from the quarry in order to build _____ 1 and 3
Calakmul.fact: This causeway may have been built to transport stone from the quarry in order to build Structures 1 and 3.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sacbe 3 extends _____ (5.0 mi) northeast from the site core and is visible from the summit of Structure 1
Calakmul.fact: Sacbe 3 extends 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) northeast from the site core and is visible from the summit of Structure 1.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: It was first discovered in _____
Calakmul.fact: It was first discovered in 1982. Sacbe 4 runs 24 kilometres (15 mi) southeast from the site core, it is also visible from the summit of Structure 1 and was discovered in 1982.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sacbe 4 runs 24 kilometres (15 mi) southeast from the site core, it is also visible from the summit of Structure 1 and was discovered in _____
Calakmul.fact: It was first discovered in 1982. Sacbe 4 runs 24 kilometres (15 mi) southeast from the site core, it is also visible from the summit of Structure 1 and was discovered in 1982.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sacbe 5 runs westwards from the main watering hole, across El Laberinto seasonal swamp and carries on for a total distance of _____ (9.9 mi) or more towards Sasilhá
Calakmul.fact: Sacbe 5 runs westwards from the main watering hole, across El Laberinto seasonal swamp and carries on for a total distance of 16 kilometres (9.9 mi) or more towards Sasilhá.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Sacbe 6 runs southwest across El Laberinto bajo and links Calakmul with El Mirador (_____ (23.77 mi) to the southwest) and, beyond it, El Tintal (an additional 30 kilometres (19 mi)
Calakmul.fact: Sacbe 6 runs southwest across El Laberinto bajo and links Calakmul with El Mirador (38.25 kilometres (23.77 mi) to the southwest) and, beyond it, El Tintal (an additional 30 kilometres (19 mi).

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: It is at least _____ (3.2 mi) long and runs across El Laberinto swamp
Calakmul.fact: It is at least 5.1 kilometres (3.2 mi) long and runs across El Laberinto swamp.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: A number of stelae were erected at its base by _____' K'awiil in 731
Calakmul.fact: A number of stelae were erected at its base by Yuknoom Took' K'awiil in 731.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Because it was built on a low hill, _____ 1 appears to be higher than Structure 2, although this is not the case
Calakmul.fact: Because it was built on a low hill, Structure 1 appears to be higher than Structure 2, although this is not the case. Structure 2 (or Structure II) is a massive north-facing pyramid temple, one of the largest in the Maya world.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Structure _____ (or Structure II) is a massive north-facing pyramid temple, one of the largest in the Maya world
Calakmul.fact: Because it was built on a low hill, Structure 1 appears to be higher than Structure 2, although this is not the case. Structure 2 (or Structure II) is a massive north-facing pyramid temple, one of the largest in the Maya world.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Its base measures _____ (390 ft) square and it stands over 45 metres (148 ft) high
Calakmul.fact: Its base measures 120 metres (390 ft) square and it stands over 45 metres (148 ft) high.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The core of the building (Structure _____A) is a triadic pyramid dating to the Late Preclassic period, with this ancient building still forming the highest point of the structure
Calakmul.fact: Structure 2 (or Structure II) is a massive north-facing pyramid temple, one of the largest in the Maya world. Its base measures 120 metres (390 ft) square and it stands over 45 metres (148 ft) high.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In the _____ a massive extension was added to the front of the pyramid, covering an earlier stucco-covered building on the north side
Calakmul.fact: In the Early Classic a massive extension was added to the front of the pyramid, covering an earlier stucco-covered building on the north side.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Three new shrines were built upon this extension (_____ 2B, 2C and 2D), each of these shrines had its own access stairway
Calakmul.fact: Three new shrines were built upon this extension (Structures 2B, 2C and 2D), each of these shrines had its own access stairway.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Structure 2 is similar in date, size and design to the _____ pyramid at El Mirador, and associated ceramics are also similar
Calakmul.fact: Structure 2 is similar in date, size and design to the El Tigre pyramid at El Mirador, and associated ceramics are also similar.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In the 8th century AD, _____ 2B was entombed under a large pyramid and a stepped facade covered the giant masks
Calakmul.fact: Structure 2 is similar in date, size and design to the El Tigre pyramid at El Mirador, and associated ceramics are also similar. In the 8th century AD, Structure 2B was entombed under a large pyramid and a stepped facade covered the giant masks.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: In the _____ a nine-room palace was built on top of the pyramid, supporting a roof comb that had painted stucco bas-relief decoration
Calakmul.fact: In the Late Classic a nine-room palace was built on top of the pyramid, supporting a roof comb that had painted stucco bas-relief decoration. The entire Late Classic palace measured 19.4 by 12 metres (64 by 39 ft).

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The entire Late Classic palace measured 19.4 by _____ (64 by 39 ft)
Calakmul.fact: The entire Late Classic palace measured 19.4 by 12 metres (64 by 39 ft).

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The front two rows of rooms (_____ 1 through to 6) were used for food preparation, metates and hearths were found in each of them
Calakmul.fact: The rooms were arranged in three groups of three, each room positioned behind the next. The front two rows of rooms (Rooms 1 through to 6) were used for food preparation, metates and hearths were found in each of them.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Structure 3 (or Structure III, also known as the _____) is southeast of Structure 4, on the east side of the Central Plaza
Calakmul.fact: Structure 3 (or Structure III, also called the Lundell Palace) is southeast of Structure 4, on the east side of the Central Plaza.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Structure 4 (or Structure IV) is a group of three temples on the east side of the _____
Calakmul.fact: Structure 3 (or Structure III, also called the Lundell Palace) is southeast of Structure 4, on the east side of the Central Plaza. Structure 4 (or Structure IV) is a group of three temples on the east side of the Central Plaza.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: It is divided into three sections, labelled _____ 4a, 4b and 4c
Calakmul.fact: It is divided into three sections, labelled Structures 4a, 4b and 4c.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: The central _____ 4b is built upon a substructure dating to the Preclassic period
Calakmul.fact: Structure 4 (or Structure IV) is a group of three temples on the east side of the Central Plaza. It is divided into three sections, labelled Structures 4a, 4b and 4c.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography
Calakmul.question: Together with _____ 6 on the opposite side of the plaza, these buildings form an E-Group that may have been used to determine the solstices and the equinoxes
Calakmul.fact: Structure 4 (or Structure IV) is a group of three temples on the east side of the Central Plaza. It is divided into three sections, labelled Structures 4a, 4b and 4c.

Calakmul.subject: World Geography

Cape Horn.fact: == Modern navigation == There are no regular commercial routes around the Horn, and modern ships carrying cargo are rarely seen.  However, a number of cruise ships routinely round the Horn when traveling from one ocean to the other.  These often stop in Ushuaia or Punta Arenas as well as Port Stanley.  Some of the small passenger vessels shuttling between Ushuaia and the Antarctic Peninsula will pass the Horn too, time and weather permitting.  === Sailing routes === A number of potential sailing routes may be followed around the tip of South America.  The Strait of Magellan, between the mainland and Tierra del Fuego, is a major—although narrow—passage, which was in use for trade well before the Horn was discovered.  The Beagle Channel (named for the ship of Charles Darwin's expedition), between Tierra del Fuego and Isla Navarino, offers a potential, though difficult route

Cape Horn.fact: The prevailing winds in latitudes below 40° south can blow from west to east around the world almost uninterrupted by land, giving rise to the "roaring forties" and the even more wild "furious fifties" and "screaming sixties".  These winds are hazardous enough that ships traveling east would tend to stay in the northern part of the forties (i.  not far below 40° south latitude); however, rounding Cape Horn requires ships to press south to 56° south latitude, well into the zone of fiercest winds.  These winds are exacerbated at the Horn by the funneling effect of the Andes and the Antarctic Peninsula, which channel the winds into the relatively narrow Drake Passage. Cape Horn.fact: Ice is a hazard to sailors venturing far below 40° south.  Although the ice limit dips south around the horn, icebergs are a significant hazard for vessels in the area.  In the South Pacific in February (summer in Southern Hemisphere), icebergs are generally confined to below 50° south; but in August the iceberg hazard can extend north of 40° south.  Even in February, the Horn is well below the latitude of the iceberg limit.  These hazards have made the Horn notorious as perhaps the most dangerous ship passage in the world; many ships have been wrecked, and many sailors have died attempting to round the Cape.  === Lighthouses === Two lighthouses are located near or in Cape Horn. Cape Horn.fact: === Lighthouses === Two lighthouses are located near or in Cape Horn.  The one located in the Chilean Navy Station is the more accessible and visited, and is commonly referred to as the Cape Horn lighthouse .  However, the Chilean Navy station, including the lighthouse (ARLS CHI-030, 55°57′49″S 67°13′14″W) and the memorial, are not located on Cape Horn (which is difficult to access either by land or sea), but on another land point about one mile east-northeast.  On Cape Horn proper is a smaller 4-metre (13-foot) fiberglass light tower, with a focal plane of 40 metres (130 feet) and a range of about 21 kilometres (13 miles).  This is the authentic Cape Horn lighthouse (ARLS CHI-006, 55°58′38″S 67°15′46″W), and as such the world's southernmost traditional lighthouse.  A few minor aids to navigation are located farther south, including one in the Diego Ramírez Islands and several in Antarctica.  === Recreational and sport sailing === Despite the opening of the Suez and Panama Canals, the Horn remains part of the fastest sailing route around the world, and so the growth in recreational long-distance sailing has brought about a revival of sailing via the Horn

Today, there are several major yacht races held regularly along the old clipper route via Cape Horn.  The first of these was the Sunday Times Golden Globe Race, which was a single-handed race; this inspired the present-day Around Alone race, which circumnavigates with stops, and the Vendée Globe, which is non-stop. Cape Horn.fact: It is a telling testament to the difficulty of conditions there that Antarctica, only 650 kilometres (400 miles) away across the Drake Passage, was discovered only as recently as 1820, despite the passage having been used as a major shipping route for 200 years.  === Historic trade route === From the 18th to the early 20th centuries, Cape Horn was a part of the clipper routes which carried much of the world's trade.  Sailing ships sailed round the Horn carrying wool, grain, and gold from Australia back to Europe; these included the windjammers in the heyday of the Great Grain Race of the 1930s.  Much trade was carried around the Horn between Europe and the Far East; and trade and passenger ships travelled between the coasts of the United States via the Horn.  The Horn exacted a heavy toll from shipping, however, owing to the extremely hazardous combination of conditions there.  The only facilities in the vicinity able to service or supply a ship, or provide medical care, were in the Falkland Islands.  The businesses there were so notorious for price-gouging that damaged ships were sometimes abandoned at Port Stanley

Cape Horn.fact: None of them were lost travelling around the Horn, but some, like the mighty Preußen, were victims of collisions in the busy English Channel.  Traditionally, a sailor who had rounded the Horn was entitled to wear a gold loop earring—in the left ear, the one which had faced the Horn in a typical eastbound passage—and to dine with one foot on the table; a sailor who had also rounded the Cape of Good Hope could place both feet on the table.  One particular historic attempt to round the Horn, that of HMS Bounty in 1788, has been immortalized in history due to the subsequent Mutiny on the Bounty.  This abortive Horn voyage has been portrayed (with varying historical accuracy) in three major motion pictures about Captain William Bligh's mission to transport breadfruit plants from Tahiti to Jamaica.  The Bounty made only 85 miles of headway in 31 days of east-to-west sailing, before giving up by reversing course and going around Africa.
